aiSummary.oneLiner: Computer vision pipeline for detecting and classifying chameleon species.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Meccha Chameleon Vision is a specialized machine learning pipeline designed to accurately detect and classify various species of chameleons from field photographs. It utilizes a fine-tuned convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a massive proprietary dataset of annotated herpetological images. The model is optimized to handle the extreme camouflage and varied lighting conditions typical of chameleon habitats. The repository includes both the training scripts and a lightweight inference API for deploying the model on edge devices in the field.
keyFeatures: Species classification: Accurately identifies over 50 distinct species and subspecies of chameleons.
Camouflage penetration: Specifically trained to detect specimens heavily camouflaged against natural backgrounds.
Edge deployment: Includes a quantized version of the model suitable for deployment on mobile devices or Raspberry Pi.
Training pipeline: Provides comprehensive scripts for augmenting data and fine-tuning the model on new species.
REST API: Offers a simple, containerized inference API for integrating the model into larger applications.

useCases.title: Field research
useCases.description: Deploy the model on mobile devices to assist biologists in identifying species during field surveys.

useCases.title: Ecological monitoring
useCases.description: Process footage from automated camera traps to monitor chameleon populations in specific habitats.

useCases.title: Educational tools
useCases.description: Integrate the API into educational apps that allow users to identify chameleons from their photos.

useCases.title: Conservation efforts
useCases.description: Use the classification data to track the spread of invasive species or the decline of endangered ones.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Herpetologists, conservationists, and computer vision researchers. It requires familiarity with Python, PyTorch, and basic machine learning principles.
